title: Correct the Standard's proposed system ownership table
recommendation: Revise the 'Proposed system ownership' section of the Secure Construction Standard: assign rule registry, findings, exceptions, scanner result interpretation and release posture to Tutela; restrict Aegis to operational fault observations supplied to Tutela; remove runtime monitoring from Vigila and record it as an unowned capability pending decision; restate Strata as schema validation, migration gating and drift detection with runtime data access as a proposed extension; restate Forma as accessible presentation patterns only and assign input validation to the application domain under Ordo and DOM sink restriction to Limen; restate Dokimos as quality evidence, independent completion verification and scanner benchmarking (planned); add Ordo (state legality) and Echelon Registry (release identity, artifact hashes, SBOM references).
rationale: Every proposed role except Limen, Folio (intent) and Praxis (partial) diverges from the repositories, and Tutela, the declared security authority, is omitted. The same repository's application-governance document already assigns security posture to Tutela.

title: Publish license terms for customer, auditor and escrow use of evidence tooling
recommendation: Decide and publish terms under which customers, auditors and escrow agents may run Echelon evidence tooling (Strata, Tutela, Dokimos, Praxis, Limen) to reproduce or verify evidence, and under which PolyForm Noncommercial dependencies in an Unbound escrow deposit may be used on a release condition. Add license files to EDF, Clarity and Unbound. Reconcile with the Standard's 'prefer MIT for original public tooling'.
rationale: All verified tools except the Registry are PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 with commercial licensing 'forthcoming'; EDF, Clarity and Unbound have no license file. Due diligence reviewers commonly ask about escrow and audit reproduction.

title: Refresh the shared-capability compliance matrix for Tutela and Strata
recommendation: Update AEGIS-FORMA-FOLIO-COMPLIANCE.md: Tutela now has an F# gate, secret scan and trace commands in source and CI (not in the 0.1.0 package); add a security-evidence column (secret scan, dependency review, SBOM, build attestation) per application.
rationale: The Tutela row says 'no executable implementation yet' (updated 2026-09-25), which is stale against tutela@476dc682 and the organization's own 2026-10-05 report.

title: Decide the SEC-DB-001 implementation path or amend the rule
recommendation: Record an explicit decision: either commission a Strata application data access package (REC-STRATA-001) or amend SEC-DB-001 to require an approved parameterized access layer plus Strata build-time SQL validation, without naming Strata as the runtime path.
rationale: SEC-DB-001 says 'all application database access through Strata', a capability no system has or specifies. Until decided, the rule cannot be implemented or evidenced.

title: Assign an owner for runtime security monitoring
recommendation: Decide who owns runtime security monitoring for Unbound (likely the Unbound operations architecture using an established monitoring product, with Aegis events as one input and Tutela RuntimeObservation intake). Do not assign it to Vigila.
rationale: The Standard's purpose includes monitoring runtime behavior, Tutela TUT-1301 to TUT-1304 require it, and no Echelon system provides it.

title: Specify a typed parameterized application data access package, or decline it explicitly
recommendation: If the organization chooses Strata for SEC-DB-001, write requirements for an F# application data access package that consumes the compiled Strata artifact: approved query definitions as files validated by 'strata validate --types', generated typed parameter and result shapes, bound parameters only, no string-composed SQL API, and an evidence record listing approved queries and their digests. Otherwise record a decision that runtime access is out of scope.
rationale: Strata already validates SQL against the schema and type-checks via PREPARE; extending it is cheaper than a new system, but nothing exists today and STRATA-DIV-001 says no implementation is implied.

title: Emit validate, check, plan and drift results as evidence records
recommendation: Add an --evidence output to validate, check, plan and drift that writes echelon.dd.evidence-record/0.1 records with the artifact digest, Strata version, PostgreSQL major, counts of matches, differs, not-compared, not-modelled, unverifiable and absent, and outcome 'indeterminate' whenever anything is unverifiable or not compared.
rationale: Strata's six-state comparison is the strongest existing evidence of database change control but is only emitted as console or JSON output without subject binding or signature.

title: Publish or remove the nuget-library distribution class
recommendation: Either publish the Strata NuGet library with a Registry release record or remove 'nuget-library' from the Registry entry.
rationale: The Registry lists nuget-library for Strata but only native CLI releases exist; a reviewer could read this as a programmatic access library.

title: Host a machine-readable registry of the Standard's SEC-* rules
recommendation: Add a versioned rule registry (for example security/RULES.json with schema) holding each SEC-* rule's owner, version, scope, threat and CWE mapping, enforcement mechanism, negative tests, evidence requirements, residual risks and failure behavior, linked to Tutela invariants and to analyzer rule ids in Dokimos and Limen.
rationale: The Standard requires these attributes per rule; Tutela already owns stable gate rule ids and the sensitive-data catalog, and is the declared single owner of security rules.

title: Extend security evidence with signatures, disclosure class, traces and residual risks
recommendation: Adopt the fields of schemas/dd/evidence-record.schema.json (signatures, record_digest, disclosure class, policy and control traces, reviews with bound identity, residual risks, lifecycle events) in the Tutela evidence schema or accept the evidence record as an input form, and make the gate verify signatures against a Tutela-governed evidence signing key trust root.
rationale: Tutela evidence carries digests but no signatures, a redacted boolean but no disclosure class, and no control or policy traces, so it cannot satisfy the Standard's 'Sign evidence' or public-report rules.

title: Define scanner result intake (SARIF and SBOM) and a portfolio CI scan profile
recommendation: Define how SAST, SCA, secret and SBOM outputs enter Tutela as evidence (SARIF 2.1.0 and SPDX or CycloneDX payloads referenced by digest, tool, rule set and database versions required), and publish a CI profile that runs tutela scan-secrets, dependency review and an open-source SAST tool in every application repository.
rationale: Tutela records that no portfolio repository runs secret scanning, dependency review or CodeQL; SEC-SUPPLY-001 and SEC-CRYPTO-001 have no evidence source.

title: Ship the F# gate in a release
recommendation: Release the Tutela F# CLI (gate, scan-secrets, trace) as a versioned, attested artifact recorded in the Echelon Registry, so other repositories can pin it.
rationale: The 0.1.0 package contains only an installer and schemas; the gate exists only in source and Tutela's own CI, so no other repository can run a pinned gate.

title: Map exceptions and invariants to SEC-* rule identifiers
recommendation: Require each SEC-EXC-* exception and each security invariant to reference the SEC-* rule ids it covers, so exceptions to the Standard are traceable in due diligence answers.
rationale: The Standard requires explicit, time-limited, approved exceptions; Tutela's exception model meets this but is not linked to the Standard's rule ids.

title: Build an F# semantic security analyzer adapter applying Tutela rules
recommendation: Promote the FSharp.Compiler.Service AST work in experiments/rule-provenance into an analyzer adapter that detects SEC-DB-001 bypasses (string-built SQL, direct driver use), SEC-EXEC-001 (dynamic loading, process construction), SEC-LANG-001 (unsafe, NativePtr, unreviewed interop) and SEC-LANG-002 (incomplete matches, warning suppression), using rule definitions owned by Tutela and emitting observations that Tutela interprets.
rationale: No F# semantic security analysis exists; Dokimos owns analyzer adapters and already has an experimental FCS scanner, while R8 requires security meaning to route to Tutela.

title: Host the scanner benchmark harness
recommendation: Add a benchmark harness measuring precision, recall, false positives and false negatives by weakness class for each scanner release, using NIST SARD and OWASP Benchmark where applicable plus F# vulnerable and safe fixtures and independently constructed holdouts, emitting versioned results as evidence records.
rationale: The Standard requires scanner validation reports; Dokimos is the measurement system with longitudinal, versioned results, and its existing verification benchmarks are a different subject.

title: Correct the README security ownership sentence
recommendation: Change 'Security remains owned by Aegis/Tutors' to state that security is owned by Tutela and that Aegis owns operational faults, matching R8.
rationale: The README contradicts R8 and the organization's ownership model, and is the kind of README text that misled the Standard's ownership table.

title: Generalize the trusted verifier to sign evidence records
recommendation: Extend the trusted verifier (DSSE, ECDSA P-256) to sign echelon.dd.evidence-record/0.1 canonical bytes and lifecycle events, keeping the signing key out of the agent's reach as today, and accept evidence record paths in 'work complete --evidence'.
rationale: Praxis already signs verification receipts with the convention the evidence architecture reuses; extending it avoids a new signing service.

title: Install a fail-closed security gate in governed repositories
recommendation: Add an optional Praxis-installed CI job that runs a pinned Tutela gate and the Tutela CI scan profile and blocks merge or release on BLOCKED or INDETERMINATE posture or on missing evidence.
rationale: The Standard assigns mandatory CI and release gates to Praxis; Praxis currently installs only its own validation workflow.

title: Populate SBOM, provenance and signature references in release records
recommendation: Advance REG-DIST-164 to REG-DIST-170 from draft, require build-provenance attestation references for every stable release, and SBOM references once release workflows generate them.
rationale: Release records already carry commit and SHA-256 per artifact but no provenance or SBOM references; several releases have attestations that are not recorded.

title: Register evidence producer capabilities
recommendation: Define capability identifiers for evidence producers (for example evidence.schema-drift, evidence.boundary-verification, evidence.secret-scan, evidence.sign) so the due diligence build and Tutela can discover producers with available, unavailable or misconfigured resolution.
rationale: The Registry is the integration model for Echelon systems but lists no evidence or security capabilities.

title: Disclaim security rule ownership and complete the Tutela projection
recommendation: State in Aegis documentation that it is not a rule registry, analyzer or scanner orchestrator, and work with Tutela to add the provenance-authority rule that lets Aegis fault observations count as evidence, mapped to the evidence record kind fault-observation.
rationale: The Standard assigns Aegis roles it does not perform; Tutela notes the Aegis projection cannot yet support Verified.

title: Add third-party script and bundle inventory to verify and emit evidence
recommendation: Extend 'limen verify --json' to inventory third-party scripts and generated bundles, include the boundary-rules digest, and emit a boundary-verification evidence record.
rationale: SEC-UI-002 requires inspecting generated bundles and inventorying third-party scripts; Limen verify is lexical over configured directories only.

title: Package deterministic export for Security Evidence Records with disclosure filtering
recommendation: Deliver the EPC-OUT deterministic export as a separate adapter package, render record digest and signature status, and filter restricted fields by disclosure class.
rationale: The Standard's assurance deliverables require reproducible reports; Folio has components and fixtures but no packaged deterministic export.

title: Document safe output patterns without claiming input safety
recommendation: Document which Forma patterns are safe for untrusted text content and which require application encoding, and state that Forma does not validate input.
rationale: The Standard assigns safe input primitives to Forma, which is HTML and CSS only.

title: Model the evidence record lifecycle and validated input types
recommendation: Provide an Ordo state model for the evidence record lifecycle in DD-ARC-003 section 3, and guidance for validated domain types at trust boundaries supporting SEC-DATA-001 and SEC-UI-001.
rationale: Ordo owns state and transition legality (TUT-1401); evidence lifecycle legality and validated input types are state questions.

title: Track evidence and exception expiry as follow-ups
recommendation: Accept follow-ups from Tutela or the due diligence build for evidence valid_until, exception expires_at and residual risk review_by dates via followup.create.
rationale: Vigila is a follow-up system of record, not runtime monitoring; this is the reasonable evidence role for it.

title: Support compiled evidence registries
recommendation: Include evidence records (JSON Lines and Markdown front matter) in the compiler's validation, link derivation and freshness checks.
rationale: DD-ARC-003 adopts the Knowledge Store approach; the compiler already checks compiled artifact freshness.

title: Correct the Strata persistence assumption in the monitoring architecture
recommendation: Replace 'Strata is mandatory as an architectural persistence dependency' with Strata's verified role (schema management, migration gating, drift detection) and assign evidence storage requirements to an explicitly chosen persistence design.
rationale: Strata provides no runtime persistence, append-only history, legal hold or evidence storage.

title: Adopt the evidence record schema in the build tool
recommendation: Validate evidence records against schemas/dd/evidence-record.schema.json, apply verification criteria V-01 to V-15 that are checkable offline, build registries/evidence-records.json, and block current-fact customer statements not supported by verified records.
rationale: The operating contract already forbids asserting current capability without support; the build tool should enforce it from evidence.
